changeability.rationale: Single chokepoints exist for cards and data (good), but the sprite design bakes URL knowledge into an ID-only helper so the plausible fix spans three files, and the naming/label rules are duplicated in the route and template layers.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:225-236 — speciesForPokemon<X> with an extra channel absorbs the real variation (hidden-ability flag, null) across three consumers
app/src/components.tsx:73 — CardList.extra covers type badges on home and the hidden-ability note without flag parameters

abstraction_design.rationale: The components and data helpers stretch to similar cases without copying (an Items page would reuse most of the Moves plumbing), held back by small duplications and one over-crowded pages file.

findings.issue: PokemonCard synthesizes the sprite URL from the species ID (api.ts:172) instead of carrying the API-provided sprites.front_default, so any sprite-source change forces widening CardData and editing both producers (getDex, speciesForPokemon).
findings.suggestion: Add a sprite (or front_default) field to CardData and populate it from the default variety's sprite URL in the two api.ts producers, keeping PokemonCard purely presentational.

findings.issue: The English-name title lookup is inlined four times (index.tsx:55,73,79,88) even though api.ts:160 already exports englishName for exactly this rule.
findings.suggestion: Replace each inline names.find(...) with englishName(resource); if a docTitle-specific fallback is needed, wrap it once.

findings.issue: The type-label fallback `typeLabels.get(x) ?? humanize(x)` is repeated in four templates (pokemon.tsx:69,260; details.tsx:34,132), so a labelling-rule change is four edits.
findings.suggestion: Return a labelFor(name) helper (or resolve labels into the data) alongside getTypeLabels in api.ts.

findings.issue: Removing the Abilities feature leaves getAbility and the Ability type (api.ts:125) as dead exports TypeScript will not flag.
findings.suggestion: When deleting a feature, grep api.ts for its accessors and types and remove them in the same change.

findings.issue: CardList's extra callback receives the item but both call sites ignore it and index back into the source array (`pokemon[i]`, `data.items[i]` at home.tsx:69-72), which is redundant and easy to desynchronize.
findings.suggestion: Have speciesForPokemon/getDex emit the extra data on each item (or use the p argument) so the callback closes over one value instead of an index.

findings.issue: englishShortEffect lives in the pages file while sibling text helpers live in api.ts, and its fallback chain (short_effect ?? flavor) is duplicated in MovePage and AbilityPage (details.tsx:29,59).
findings.suggestion: Move englishShortEffect to api.ts next to latestEnglishFlavor and add a single effectText(resource) helper both pages call.

findings.issue: details.tsx bundles Move, Ability, Types and Type pages; adding a resource page would grow an already mixed file (each page is independently removable, but the file's purpose is unclear).
findings.suggestion: Split into pages per resource (moves.tsx, types.tsx, abilities.tsx) or state a grouping convention; new resources get their own file.

findings.issue: getDex derives per-Pokémon types via an inverse index built from the type endpoint rather than from Pokémon data — indirect, and a change to how types are sourced ripples through this hidden dependency.
findings.suggestion: Note the choice in a comment or fetch types from the default Pokémon where the rest of the species summary is assembled.

summary: This is a small, idiomatic Hono + htmx app with one clean data seam (api.ts) and genuinely reusable card/section abstractions, so most cross-cutting changes — data source, caching, new resource pages — are easy. The friction is concentrated in card sprites (URL synthesized from an ID instead of carried from the API, so the plausible fix spans three files) and small duplicated lookups in the route and template layers. Feature removal works but touches four files, which is typical of this routing structure rather than a design flaw.
